chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorced woman may apply kohl, dye her hair, use perfume, and wear whatever clothes she desires.
Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Perhaps Allah will bring about after that a new situation; perhaps she will come to his mind, so he will remarry her.'

key_terms.فَيُرَاجِعَهَا: So he will remarry her / return to her
key_terms.لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ: Perhaps Allah will bring about (a new situation)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding a divorced woman's adornment and clothing during her waiting period in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi, narrated through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies that a divorced woman retains full freedom of adornment during her 'iddah (waiting period), countering restrictive interpretations. The rationale links her physical beauty to the Quranic concept of hope for reconciliation, suggesting that her attractiveness may prompt the husband to exercise his right of return. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the waiting period is not a period of seclusion or mourning, but a time of potential restoration of the marital bond.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The divorced woman should apply Kohl, and hair dye, and perfume, and wear whatsoever she so desires to from the clothes, because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [65:1] Perhaps Allah may after that bring about reunion.
Perhaps she would occur in his self so he would revert back to her’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A divorced woman can use kohl, dyes, perfumes and wear whatever she likes
because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, . .perhaps Allah may bring about something thereafter.’ Perhaps something happens in his mind and he goes back to her.’”
